company_name: The People's Insurance Company (Group) of China Limited (PICC Group)
model: P&C-led insurance group FCFE at cost of equity, net debt held at zero (engine route)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: long-run growth of the earning base -- original premiums +6.5% in FY2025 (industry +7.4%), insurance revenue +6.1% FY2025 and +2.4% H1 2026 (industry premiums +3.2% H1 2026), investment assets +5.1% in six months to RMB1,997,723M; mid-single-digit, fading to 3% terminal. Revenue CAGRs straddle the IFRS 17 break, EPS and NI CAGRs start from pre-rally years and end on a peak, and equity CAGRs carry OCI; none is used as the growth input.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 3yr CAGR (11.7%) diverges from EPS 3yr CAGR (23.7%) by more than 30%: FY2022 EPS 0.55 was pre-rally and pre-IFRS 17, FY2025 EPS 1.04 is a peak-cycle year. Revenue CAGRs (2.8%) are depressed by the IFRS 4 -> IFRS 17 revenue break at FY2023. The warning is noted and all series are set aside in favour of the ROE normalisation in inputs.notes.

scenario_narratives.base: China's dominant P&C insurer (31.6% share, double its nearest rival) wrapped in a state-controlled group with sub-scale but fast-improving life and health arms, valued on the dividends it can actually pay to a minority H-shareholder. Attributable profit normalises from the FY2025 / H1 2026 market-rally peak to ~12% ROE (~RMB44bn), keeping most of the structural P&C underwriting gain, grows with premiums and the investment book at 4.5% fading to 3%, and the payout climbs from 24% toward 40% against the strongest solvency of the big four. Capitalised at a 10% CNY cost of equity with the terminal capped at 14x FCFE, the H-share is worth roughly 0.7x book -- above a price that discounts it at 0.56x book, ~4x FY2025 earnings and below the market value of its listed PICC P&C stake alone.
scenario_narratives.bull: The combined ratio holds at 94-95%, investment yields stay near 5%, PICC Life and PICC Health turn EV growth into visible profit, and the payout reaches the 50% peer level; the H-share rerates toward ~0.9x book, where the A-share trades.
scenario_narratives.bear: An H2 2026 equity drawdown and catastrophe losses erase the second half, falling CGB yields expose negative-spread risk in the life/health books, motor competition compresses P&C margins and the payout stays in the low 20s; the stock settles at 10x a flat dividend stream at ~0.45x book -- below today's price.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value a Chinese insurance group on the cash it distributes to minority shareholders, not on IFRS 17 net income (one-third investment variance) and not on OCF (premium float). Attributable profit before tax after the structurally low 16.5% effective rate is the earnings measure -- consolidated PBT scaled by the 74% attributable share, so the 26% of profit owned by minorities in PICC P&C, PICC Life and PICC Health is charged once, inside the margin -- and the payout ratio, calibrated to the FY2025 dividend and the H1 2026 interim increase, sets how much of it must be retained. Debt interest is inside that measure, so net debt is zero. FY2025 and H1 2026 margins are peak-cycle and are normalised to the FY2019-25 mean ROE of ~12.4%, keeping the P&C underwriting improvement but reverting the investment-yield windfall. CROSS-CHECKS: (1) Book: attributable equity RMB341,037M at H1 2026 = RMB7.71/share; the H-share price is 0.56x book, the A-share 0.98x; the base value of ~RMB5.2 is ~0.67x book, which for a 12-12.5% ROE at a 10% cost of equity is conservative (a residual-income P/B at those inputs would be above 1x). (2) Sum of parts: the Group's 68.98% of PICC P&C (2328.HK, 22,242M shares at HKD15.22 = HKD338.5bn = RMB288bn) is worth RMB199bn = RMB4.50/share = HKD5.28 at market -- MORE than the Group's own H-share price of HKD5.06 -- before PICC Life (EV 147,937 x 80% = 118bn) and PICC Health (EV 40,793 x 95.45% = 39bn), which the H price therefore values at less than zero. A look-through of ~RMB356bn (RMB8.05/share, HKD9.45) is not used as the headline because holdco discounts on Chinese financial groups are persistent and the P&C stake is not for sale; it is the ceiling the bull case approaches, not the base. (3) Retained earnings are charged as lost cash (the engine's retention plug), which understates value if retained capital compounds book at 12%+; the rising payout path is the compromise, and its sensitivity is stated in inputs.notes.
key_risks_to_valuation: Capital-markets leverage: 22.3% of a RMB2.0tn investment book in equities (up from 18.2%); total investment income was 46% of H1 2026 revenue growth and Q1 2026 attributable profit fell 31.4% on markets alone
Reinvestment / negative-spread risk: net investment yield 3.5% (FY2025) and 1.7% unannualised in H1 2026 against a 10-year CGB near 1.8% and legacy 3-3.5% guarantees in PICC Life and PICC Health

P&C underwriting cycle: the combined ratio improved 98.8% -> 97.5% -> 94.0% (H1 2026); a return to 98-99% through motor price competition or a catastrophe-heavy year removes roughly a third of normalised attributable profit
Catastrophe exposure as China's largest agricultural and catastrophe insurer (480m+ people covered; agricultural and liability lines already run combined ratios above 100%)

Payout policy is a state-shareholder decision (MOF 60.8%, SSF 12.7%); the rise from 21% to 40% is a judgment supported by the +46.7% interim, not guidance -- held flat at 21% the base value falls ~40%
NCI share assumed constant at 74%; a buy-in of PICC P&C minorities would raise attributable profit but consume capital, and a sell-down would do the reverse
A/H structure: the H-share has traded at a 40%+ discount to the A-share; the model values the H at the H price and there is no mechanism forcing convergence

Q3 2026 results (c. 29 Oct 2026) are the first evidence on H2 2026; the base assumes a weak H2 (~12.6bn attributable) and the bear a near-zero H2 -- an H2 as strong as H1 would lift the FY2026 anchor by ~RMB20bn of attributable profit

Model risk: FCFE charges all retained earnings as lost; if retained capital compounds book at the historical 12%+ ROE, value is understated by a wide margin (see the book and sum-of-parts cross-checks)

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (HKEX regular close); 52-week range 4.63-7.63. FX: Yahoo HKDCNY=X, inverted, same date; A-share parity from 601319.SS; PICC P&C stake marked off 2328.HK same close
data_sources.financials: 1339.HK_Metrics.csv (core_metrics, RMB millions, FY2018-FY2025 + H1/Q1/Q3 interims through H1 2026) and the kpis table (NetIncomeIncludingNCI, TotalEquity, DividendsPaid, ProfitBeforeTax, InsuranceRevenue); FY2025 Annual Report (consolidated income statement, dividends per 10 shares, subsidiaries table 68.98% / 80% / 95.45%, bonds payable, Note on leases); H1 2026 Interim Report (share capital table, segment PBT, income tax 12,109, investment assets 1,997,723 and yields 3.7% / 1.7% unannualised with a 5.0% three-year average, solvency 197.7% / 246.6%, PICC Life EV 147,937 and PICC Health EV 40,793, NCI 121,696, equity 341,037, interim dividend RMB0.11)
data_sources.qualitative: 1339.HK_Analysis.json (2026-10-16): segment mix, P&C market share and combined ratio, life/health NBV growth, Five Priorities investment mandate, solvency, bull/bear cases, sell-side targets HKD6.8-8.2

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2025 total revenue as the CSV defines it (FY2025 AR consolidated income statement: insurance revenue 570,717 + total investment income ~93,000 + other). IFRS 17 insurance revenue is service-margin recognition, not premiums: original premiums income was 738,333 in FY2025 (+6.5%). H1 2026 revenue 355,169 vs 324,122 (+9.6%), of which total investment income 66,327 vs 40,758 (+62.7%) on an unannualised total investment yield of 3.7% vs 2.6% -- the H1 2026 step-up is an A-share rally, not premium growth (insurance revenue +2.4%). H2 2025 revenue was 345,132.
inputs.share_count_basis: 44,223,990,583 shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (H1 2026 interim report: 'no change in the total number of shares and the share capital' during the period; MOF 26,906,570,608 A + SSF 5,605,582,779 A + HKSCC Nominees 8,707,410,103 H among the top holders). No share-based payment scheme, no convertibles, no treasury shares: basic = diluted (FY2025 AR diluted EPS 1.00 vs basic 1.04 reflects a subsidiary-level dilution adjustment, not Group instruments). A and H shares rank pari passu for dividends, so the per-share value is on the total count and the H-share price is compared against it. Held FLAT.
inputs.net_debt_treatment: Held at ZERO, the banks/insurers convention in this folder (LGEN.L, PRU, GL, 0998.HK, 1336.HK). Bonds payable RMB41,590M at 30 June 2026 (41,806 at FY2025) are capital supplementary bonds issued by the insurance subsidiaries as Tier 2 regulatory capital, whose coupon is deducted inside profit before tax, so the flows already pay for them. Securities sold under repurchase agreements (141,482 at H1 2026, 180,763 at FY2025) are investment-operations funding and are netted inside the investment-yield definition. Cash 53,013 is policyholder and investment-portfolio liquidity inside RMB1.998tn of investment assets, not shareholder surplus. Solvency surplus (comprehensive 246.6%, core 197.7% at 30 June 2026) is the regulatory buffer and is NOT added back; it is what lets the payout ratio rise in the base case.
inputs.last_fcf_note: FY2025 dividends declared to Group shareholders, RMB9,729M = RMB0.22/share (interim 0.075 + final 0.145, i.e. RMB2.20 per 10 shares, +22.2%) x 44,224M shares, 21.1% of attributable net profit of 46,207 (FY2025 AR). This is the observed FCFE: the only cash a Group shareholder receives. OCF less capex (CSV 113,905 for FY2025) is premium float being invested and is not free cash; attributable net income is 74% of consolidated profit because PICC P&C (68.98% owned), PICC Life (80%) and PICC Health (95.45%) carry large minorities. The identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income is therefore deliberately not satisfied; reported_fcf is retained for auditability only.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report: no share-based payment, share option or share incentive scheme at Group level (kpis EquityAwardTaxes 0 in every year, ShareRepurchases 0 in every year). State-controlled (Ministry of Finance 60.8%, SSF 12.7%) A/H-share insurer; SBC is genuinely zero, so house and street bases coincide and band_position is null.
inputs.buyback_note: No buybacks in any year of the history; the count has been 44,224M since the 2018 A-share IPO. The flat count is a fact, not a modelling convention that needs funding.
inputs.fx_note: Statements and flows are RMB (CNY) millions; the HKEX H-share quote is HKD. fx_rate converts model to quote: 1 CNY = 1.1738 HKD, from Yahoo HKDCNY=X 0.8519 on 2026-10-16T08:21Z (inverted). Parity check against the Shanghai A-share (601319.SS, same economic rights): RMB7.58 x 1.1738 = HKD8.90 against the observed H-share HKD5.06, i.e. the H trades at a 43% discount to the A (AH premium ~76%, one of the widest among the big-four insurers). The check proves the rate's direction and magnitude, not price parity. All per-share values are computed in CNY and converted; canonical intrinsic_value / weighted_iv / entry_price are HKD, comparable to current_price, with *_cny siblings. refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z HKEX regular close (Friday, 16:08 HKT); 52-week range 4.63-7.63, i.e. the price sits near the bottom of its range, 34% below the high, despite H1 2026 attributable profit +40.4%, ahead of Q3 2026 results due around 29 October 2026
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of EQUITY 10.0%, built in CNY because the flows are CNY: China 10-year government bond ~1.8% (mid-2026, approximate; no live CGB quote through the Yahoo chart endpoint) + beta ~1.25 x 6.5% China ERP = ~9.9%, rounded to 10.0%. Half a point BELOW the 10.5% used for 1336.HK (New China Life) and 0998.HK because PICC's earnings have a large non-market component -- PICC P&C underwriting profit (12,535 in FY2025 at a 97.5% combined ratio; 94.0% in H1 2026) and float income on a short-tail book -- and because core solvency at 197.7% is far above NCI's 126%, so the payout path is not capital-constrained. Not lower than 10% because 22.3% of a RMB2tn investment book is in equities (up from 18.2%), Q1 2026 attributable profit fell 31.4% on markets alone, and the A/H structure adds a governance and capital-controls premium H-share investors demonstrably price (43% A/H discount). One rate across all three scenarios; cyclicality is carried in the bear path and its weight.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not applicable: lease liabilities RMB1,881M at FY2025 against RMB2.0tn of assets; the IFRS 16 charge sits inside operating expenses already deducted in profit before tax.
inputs.nci_treatment: Material and charged ONCE, inside the margin. Non-controlling interests are RMB121,696M of equity (26.3% of total equity 462,733 at H1 2026) and take 26-27% of consolidated profit: attributable / consolidated net profit was 72.4% (FY2023), 74.2% (FY2024), 74.0% (FY2025), 73.7% (H1 2026). The engine's ebitda_margin_path is therefore ATTRIBUTABLE profit before tax as % of revenue = consolidated PBT x 74% / revenue, so after the cash tax rate the flow ties to attributable net income (FY2025: 73,952 x 0.74 = 54,724 pre-tax -> x (1 - 15.6%) = 46,207 attributable, exactly the reported figure). No separate NCI deduction is made in the bridge. The 74% share is held constant: PICC P&C's weight in Group profit (41,212 of 62,945 segment PBT in H1 2026) is stable and no buy-in or sell-down of the P&C stake is assumed.
inputs.notes: MODEL: FCFE at cost of equity on a P&C-led Chinese insurance group, run through the component engine with net debt at zero -- the pattern used for LGEN.L / PRU / GL / IAG.AX / 1336.HK in this folder (SKILL.md routing row: insurer). Not the owner-FCF DCF: OCF of RMB64-119bn a year is premium float, and EBITDA does not exist. Not the routing table's default BVPS x exit-P/B either, for comparability with 1336.HK (built the same day) and because the dividend is the one flow a minority H-shareholder of a 73.5% state-owned group actually receives; BVPS x P/B and a sum-of-parts on the listed P&C stake are the CROSS-CHECKS (see valuation_philosophy). ENGINE MAPPING: revenue = total revenue as the CSV defines it (insurance revenue + total investment income + other); ebitda_margin_path = ATTRIBUTABLE profit before tax as % of revenue (consolidated PBT x 74% NCI share -- see nci_treatment): FY2023 4.4%, FY2024 8.26%, FY2025 8.18%, H1 2026 13.1%; sbc_pct_path = 0 (SBC-zero SOE); da = 0 (D&A ~5.1bn is inside the expense base); cash_tax_rate = 16.5% (FY2025 ETR 15.6%, FY2024 18.0%, FY2023 8.2%, FY2022 16.3%, FY2021 14.7%, H1 2026 19.2%; the low rate is structural -- tax-exempt CGB interest and dividend income -- and the H1 2026 rate is the higher-tax P&C segment's weight in a strong half); capex_pct_path is the RETENTION plug = the share of after-tax attributable profit kept as solvency capital and new-business strain, so FCFE = attributable net income x payout ratio, with capex_pct = margin x (1 - tax) x (1 - payout). NORMALISATION: FY2024-25 doubled attributable profit from the FY2019-23 RMB20-24bn range to 42-46bn through two things -- a structural P&C underwriting improvement (combined ratio 98.8% -> 97.5% -> 94.0% in H1 2026, underwriting profit +119%) and an A-share rally (total investment yield 5.6% in FY2025 vs a three-year average of 5.0% and a net investment yield of 3.5%, falling). H1 2026 (attributable 37,451, +40.4%; total investment income +62.7%) is peak-cycle and is NOT annualised. ROE on average attributable equity ran 13.2% (FY2019), 10.4%, 10.2%, 11.1%, 9.6% (FY2023), 16.5%, 16.0% (FY2025): FY2019-25 mean 12.4%. The base path settles at ~12-12.5% ROE from FY2027 (attributable NI ~44bn on ~360bn of equity, EPS ~RMB1.0), i.e. it keeps most of the P&C underwriting gain but reverts the investment gains to the three-year-average yield. PAYOUT: 21.1% in FY2025 is the lowest of the big four (NCI 23.5%, China Life ~35%, Ping An 40%+, CPIC ~35%) despite the strongest solvency (core 197.7%, comprehensive 246.6%); the interim was lifted 46.7% to RMB0.11 in H1 2026 and FY2025 DPS +22.2%, under the SOE market-value-management push. The base lifts the payout from 24% (FY2026) to 40% by FY2033 and holds it; this is the single largest judgment in the model -- held flat at 21% the base value falls by roughly 40%. H2 2026 is NOT extrapolated from H1: the share price has fallen 34% from its 52-week high ahead of the Q3 2026 release, so the base assumes H2 2026 attributable profit of ~12.6bn (vs H1 37.5bn; H2 2025 19.5bn, which itself contained a Q4 2025 loss of ~0.8bn), and the bear assumes an H2 close to break-even.
inputs.transition_note: FY2022 and earlier rows are IFRS 4 / IAS 39 (revenue is premiums-based: 615,732 in FY2022); FY2023 onward are IFRS 17 / IFRS 9 (553,467 in FY2023 is the presentation break, not an operating fall). Attributable equity FY2022 221,771 vs FY2023 243,206 straddles the restatement. No series spanning FY2022 is used as an anchor; the base is FY2025 and the H1 2026 run-rate, with ROE on attributable equity (comparable across regimes) as the normalisation gauge.

bear.narrative: An H2 2026 A-share drawdown turns fair-value gains into losses and a catastrophe-heavy second half (floods/typhoons on China's largest agricultural and catastrophe book) pushes the P&C combined ratio back toward 99%: FY2026 revenue -1%, margin 7.0% (attributable NI ~38.5bn, i.e. H2 ~1bn after the 37.5bn H1 -- the Q4 2025 shape stretched over a half). FY2027: the 10-year CGB slides toward 1.5%, net investment yield (3.5% FY2025, 1.7% unannualised H1 2026) keeps compressing against legacy 3-3.5% guarantees at PICC Life and PICC Health, motor pricing competition from Ping An P&C re-intensifies, and the margin falls to 5.0% (NI ~27bn, ROE ~7.5% -- the FY2023 level). Growth 2-3% thereafter as motor volumes stagnate and the life/health franchise stays sub-scale at ~4% share. Payout held at 22-28% through FY2033 as management prioritises the life/health build-out and the state shareholders accept the status quo; 30% by FY2035. Tax 17%. Terminal min(Gordon 10.0%/2.5%, 10x FCFE) -- the H-share stays at ~0.45x book.

base.narrative: FY2026: revenue +3% (H1 +9.6% on the A-share rally; H2 assumed weak against H2 2025, consistent with the 34% share-price fall into the Q3 release) at an 8.7% attributable pre-tax margin = attributable NI ~50.1bn (H1 37.5bn + H2 ~12.6bn), dividend ~12.0bn (DPS ~0.27 = 0.11 interim + ~0.16 final, +24%, payout 24%). FY2027: revenue +2% and margin normalises to 7.5% as total investment yield reverts from 5.6% toward the 5.0% three-year average while the P&C combined ratio holds ~96-97%: attributable NI ~44bn, ROE ~12.2% -- the FY2019-25 mean. FY2028 onward: revenue +4.5% with original premiums (non-motor P&C, life regular premium, health/nursing care) and the investment book, margin 7.6-7.8%, growth fading to 3% by FY2035. Payout rises 2-3pp a year from 24% to 40% by FY2033 as the SOE market-value-management push continues against 197.7% core solvency; held at 40%, below China Life / CPIC, because the Group also funds PICC Life and PICC Health growth capital. Tax 16.5%. Terminal min(Gordon 10.0%/3%, 14x FCFE = 5.6x earnings at a 40% payout, ~0.7x book at a 12.5% ROE) -- the cap binds just below Gordon.

bull.narrative: H2 2026 markets hold: FY2026 revenue +6%, margin 9.6% (attributable NI ~57bn, H2 ~19bn in line with H2 2025), then the P&C combined ratio stays at the 94-95% H1 2026 level as 'Vehicle Insurance Made Easy' pricing discipline and AI claims efficiency hold, total investment yield settles at ~5% rather than reverting, and the margin normalises only to 8.6-8.8% (ROE ~14%). PICC Life NBV compounds on the regular-premium shift (EV +19% in six months) and PICC Health nursing care keeps growing 50%+, so the life/health 'second curve' becomes a visible profit contributor. Core solvency near 200% lets the payout reach 50% by FY2034 -- the China Life / CPIC level. Terminal min(Gordon 10.0%/3.5%, 16x FCFE) -- a rerating toward ~0.9x book, where the A-share already trades.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 14x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: 22.3% of a RMB2tn investment book is in equities, Q1 2026 attributable profit fell 31.4% on markets alone, the 34% share-price fall into the Q3 2026 release says the market expects a weak H2, and the H-share's 43% discount to the A has no convergence mechanism. Not raised to 1336.HK's 30% because PICC's earnings have a large non-market P&C underwriting component, core solvency at 197.7% is far above the level at which the payout path would be capital-constrained, and the Group has not had a loss-making year in the history. Bull cut from 35% to 25% because it needs the combined ratio, the investment yield and a doubling of the payout ratio all to hold at once, under a state shareholder whose dividend policy is a policy decision. 25/50/25 matches LGEN.L, PRU and 0998.HK.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
